entities.evidence: Genesis 5:25 identifies this Lamech as Methuselah’s son, and 5:29 names his son Noah. The Lamech of Genesis 4:18 is Methushael’s son.

name_review_base.evidence: Genesis 5:25 identifies this Lamech as Methuselah’s son, and 5:29 names his son Noah. The Lamech of Genesis 4:18 is Methushael’s son.

analysis.evidence: לֶמֶךְ is the subject of וַיְחִי. The following numerals give the duration of Lamech’s life before he fathered a son, 182 years.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix
analysis.sense: live for a stated length of time

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לֶמֶךְ with the derivation left open.
draft.definition: A Hebrew masculine personal name, borne here by the son of Methuselah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:25 names the child in וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת לָמֶךְ, “and he fathered Lamech.”

analysis.evidence: Genesis 5:25 identifies Lamech as Methuselah’s son. In 5:28, לֶמֶךְ is the subject of וַיְחִי, “he lived,” and remains the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד בֵּן, “he fathered a son.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׁתַּיִם agrees with the feminine noun שָׁנָה and supplies the units in Lamech’s age: two plus eighty plus one hundred years.
In שְׁתַּיִם וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה, two and eighty make eighty-two years. The following וּמְאַת שָׁנָה adds one hundred years, giving Lamech’s age as 182.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ prefixed to a cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁתַּיִם וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה, the singular noun supplies the unit for “eighty-two.” The following וּמְאַת שָׁנָה adds a hundred years, giving Lamech’s age as 182 when he fathered a son.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מְאַת stands in construct before שָׁנָה ‘year’. The conjunction adds a hundred years to the preceding eighty-two, giving Lamech’s age as 182 when he fathered a son.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ + feminine singular construct numeral מְאַת ‘a hundred’.

analysis.evidence: In וּמְאַת שָׁנָה, “and a hundred years,” מְאַת is the construct form of “hundred” and שָׁנָה supplies the unit. These hundred years complete the count of 182 years that Lamech lived before he fathered a son.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: לֶמֶךְ is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and בֵּן is its direct object. After stating Lamech’s age, the verse says that he fathered a son.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד בֵּן, “he fathered a son,” בֵּן is the direct object of וַיּוֹלֶד and denotes Lamech’s male child.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, without a prefix or suffix.
